content.title: About
content.content: Bologna is a cooked‑smoked sausage made from beef and pork, seasoned with spices and flavorings. In the reduced‑sodium version the salt content is cut to 0.5 g per 100 g, making it more suitable for people watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Although called “Italian sausage,” the modern bologna originated in the United States in the early 20th century.
Sodium reduction is achieved by replacing part of the salt with potassium chloride and using natural flavor enhancers.
Bologna is commonly used in sandwiches, salads, and as an ingredient in hot dishes such as pasta.
The classic recipe blends beef, pork, and sometimes veal, giving it a distinctive flavor.
Reduced‑sodium bologna can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks after opening.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 15 g of high‑quality animal protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron supports normal hemoglobin levels and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps control blood pressure and lessens strain on the cardiovascular system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bologna supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef or pork.

items.title: Nitrite content
items.content: Like most smoked sausages, bologna can contain nitrites, which are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Despite lower sodium, the product remains relatively fatty; portion control is advised for those monitoring fat intake.

items.title: Potassium level
items.content: People with kidney disease should watch potassium chloride intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice bologna thinly for sandwiches, add it to salads, use it in hot dishes (pasta, casseroles) or grill it. Let the slices reach room temperature before serving to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bologna in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +4 °C. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
